title: Trend Following too complicated- - Systematic Investor 296

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Trend Following too complicated- - Systematic Investor 296.docx

speakers: Mark Rzepczynski (systematic researcher, caption 'Mark with sininsky')
summary: Mark and Niels discuss the SG Capital Consulting investor survey, mid-May 2024 CTA results, de-globalisation and dispersion, using economic data in trend models, and the VUCA risk framework. Conclusion: in a disordered, high-VUCA world follow price trends with diversification and ensembles; industry complexity is partly marketing.

coverage.note: crypto heist story; market plumbing; SG survey intro
SG survey: fixed income relative value, CTA non-trend, currency
currency volatility; discretionary vs quant macro and CTA trend
strategy interest table; Dow 40,000; trend update
index numbers; China vs India stock markets
lower correlations; inflation regimes for trend
manager skill; trend vs forecast; inflation dispersion
narrative problem; economic data in trend models

completeness_estimate: 0.85 - the first reader captured the survey findings, de-globalisation view, macro-vs-price debate and the VUCA mapping well; missed several smaller points (storytelling reason, survey vs flows, magazine-cover contrarian signal, sector composition caveat, yield-curve ambiguity, uncertainty and risk-taking) and blended two speakers in one claim.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: The False Consensus Effect
claims.claim: False consensus effect: people in similar educational and media bubbles believe one view is universal, so new information produces a large market reaction and dislocations.
claims.conditions: narrative-driven markets; amplified by social media

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: the plumbing matters in how we trade markets
claims.claim: Market plumbing (clearing, transparent rules) matters; futures markets are transparent and need minimal regulation for liquidity, unlike crypto where opaque money movement creates arbitrage and structural risks.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: the number one shift in interest to the positive uh was called fixed income relative value
claims.claim: Per the SG Capital Consulting survey (472 responses, 315 firms), the largest rise in investor interest vs fall 2023 was fixed income relative value, linked to high rate volatility (MOVE index) and a higher-rate regime with more dispersion.
claims.testable: yes - MOVE index and relative value returns

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: there's also this decline in CTA non- Trend
claims.claim: Interest fell in currency strategies and non-trend CTAs (e.g. short-term managers) even though dispersion and central bank divergence should favour them; trend followers had positive years five years in a row and made more P&L in currencies in the last 6-12 months.
claims.indicator: currency sector P&L for trend followers

correction.issue: Mixes two speakers and their opposite reactions. Mark says he was surprised by the falls in currency and CTA non-trend interest. Niels says he is not surprised by CTA non-trend (short-term managers have done poorly; interest should go to trend, positive five years in a row) and only a little surprised by currency, because trend followers have made more currency P&L over the past 6-12 months (like cocoa suddenly coming alive), while currency managers must first make money to attract interest.
correction.fix: Mark: interest in currency and non-trend CTA strategies fell, which surprised him given central bank divergence and dispersion. Niels: not surprised by non-trend CTA (short-term managers have done poorly and trend has had five positive years in a row); somewhat surprised by currency since trend followers have made more currency P&L in the last 6-12 months.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: volatility and currencies are always relatively low versus you you know equities Commodities
claims.claim: Currencies have lower volatility than equities, commodities and bonds, so professional users need more leverage in currencies and have less interest because they move less.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: the Goldilocks of macro strategies
claims.claim: Investors seek discretionary global macro (interest about 50% in the survey throughout) which is hard to find; quantitative global macro is less liked; CTA trend sits in between as a substitute with convexity and global exposure, a 'poor man's global macro'.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: V trading has just dropped off completely
claims.claim: Volatility trading interest fell in the survey after a lack of sustained volatility, risk premia strategies attract very little interest despite being taught in finance, and long equity interest was low despite good equity returns.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the 128 year old Dow Jones Industrial Average has crossed 40,000 points for the first time
claims.claim: On 16 May 2024 the Dow crossed 40,000, 873 trading days after first closing above 30,000 and up ~40% from its Sept 2022 low; trend followers recovered with equities, metals and some energy but May was still negative for CTAs.
claims.indicator: Dow Jones Industrial Average, CTA indices

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: s gen CTA index down 2.23% for the month
claims.claim: Mid-May 2024 numbers (transcript garbles YTD figures): BTOP50 -2.1% May, SG CTA -2.23%, SG Trend -2.75% (YTD +11.17%), short-term traders -0.19% (+3.39% YTD), MSCI World ~+5% May (+9.45% YTD), World government bonds +1.28%, S&P 500 +5.3% (+11.66% YTD).
claims.indicator: BTOP50, SG CTA, SG Trend, MSCI World, S&P 500

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: the wealth creation in the Indian stock market is much greater than what we've seen in the Chinese market over the very long run
claims.claim: Chinese equity growth has not translated into stock market wealth creation versus India, and the 2024 Chinese rally followed government and state entity buying and changed perceptions.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: a movement from multilateralism to bilateralism
claims.claim: The liberal order (free trade, free capital flow, WTO) is eroding via sanctions, tariffs (continued by Biden) and capital controls, moving from multilateralism to bilateralism, causing more price dispersion, dislocation, uncertainty, lower cross-market correlation and more tail risk, so convexity and global macro are favoured.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: A New World Order we'll call it the age of disorder those correlations are going to go down
claims.claim: In the age of disorder, equity indices across countries correlate less, creating more opportunities to trade countries separately.
claims.testable: yes - rolling correlation of country indices

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we can have low inflation like we had uh say from 80s up until 1999 but it wasn't stable and actually that was a pretty good environment for Trend following
claims.claim: Low but unstable inflation (1980s-1999) was good for trend following while low and stable inflation in the 2000s-2010s was harder; if inflation is neither low nor stable now it may create opportunities.
claims.testable: yes - trend returns by inflation volatility regime

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: most of the studies uh that look at Financial skill would sort of say that the managers themselves believe they have more skill
claims.claim: Studies show managers overestimate their skill, so forecasting the world's moves is hard, and a rules-based approach is preferred.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: these price trends might last longer than what we expect and that's would be the opportunity
claims.claim: If the world becomes more disordered, price trends may last longer; tariffs and trade barriers prevent price equilibration so inflation dispersion across countries and trends persist.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: if they're right then most likely we're going to be right as well and if they're wrong they hopefully we'll have less exposure
claims.claim: A trend system will get long on the way to a discretionary forecast (S&P from 5,000 to 6,000) if the forecast is right and stays small if it is wrong; few forecast the previous year's equity highs, so consensus was wrong.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: the narrative for Trend following is much more difficult than the narrative for a discretionary Global macro guy
claims.claim: Narrative drives marketing and investment decisions; non-predictive trend following (go long if trend is up, short if down) is a harder story to sell to institutions than a discretionary macro story.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: these macro data becoming or economic data becoming actually the input into some Trend following models
claims.claim: Some trend managers (AQR) use roughly 50/50 price and economic signals; systematic macro that combines story and rules was popular ten years ago, worked for a while and then many stopped working.
claims.testable: yes - blend of price and macro signals

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: the macro Trends will often Drive price trends
claims.claim: Macro trends drive price trends but do not always precede them and may only reinforce; the yield curve shape, consumer sentiment and PMIs tell something about bonds and equities, and a large part of the equity premium accrues on macro announcements (FOMC, unemployment).
claims.indicator: yield curve, consumer sentiment, PMI, announcement-day returns

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: what I like about price is there's only one and and so it for me price is truth
claims.claim: Niels prefers price because there is only one price while economic data and the yield curves are ambiguous; COVID shutdown followed by 50-60% equity gains made no sense economically.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: if you were used the shape of the yield curve as an indicator for your model you probably would have sort of cut your Equity exposure
claims.claim: The inverted yield curve and the COVID economic data would have cut equity exposure and missed gains, but blending macro and price trends gives smoother returns, lower risk and higher Sharpe; systematic macro is still in its infancy.
claims.indicator: yield curve inversion, macro trends vs price trends blend
claims.direction: blend macro and price trend models

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: vuka which is uh stands for volatility uncertainty complexity and ambiguity
claims.claim: VUCA (volatility, uncertainty, complexity, ambiguity) is a framework for risk; current equity volatility is low and bond volatility, though high, has declined, making it a lower-risk environment surprisingly.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: uncertainty would mean this is I got to say that that's subjective because I can't count the event
claims.claim: Volatility is countable risk; uncertainty is non-countable (a pandemic, a recession with fewer than a dozen post-WWII samples versus 30 needed), so yield-curve recession signals are subjective; political uncertainty indices were lower than two years earlier.
claims.indicator: political uncertainty indices, yield curve sample size

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: because you can't come up with good factors or stories to explain the phenomena
claims.claim: Complexity (number of factors needed to explain returns, e.g. PCA) and ambiguity (unstable factor betas such as inflation beta) both raise risk; in high VUCA follow price trends because other relationships may be compromised.
claims.indicator: PCA factor count, inflation beta stability

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: if I have high volatility I want to I want to try to increase uh diversification okay makes sense if I have high uncertainty I probably want to put stop losses
claims.claim: Matching VUCA to design: diversify for volatility, stop losses for uncertainty, simple models with added factors for complexity, ensembles for ambiguity (e.g. mixing long- and short-term trend).

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: the addition of complexity is is uh driven by two causes
claims.claim: The industry is adding complexity to adapt to new phenomena (pandemic, zero rates) and for marketing, to create an alpha gap versus managers running the same models; whether complexity helps is unproven.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: engineering under under uncertainty
claims.claim: Model builders behave like engineers designing under uncertainty (unlike bridge builders who know the stresses), adding complexity to cope with market uncertainty rather than from physics envy.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I think it's because they're the best storytellers right uh and they have a lot of uh personality some of these discretionary Global macrom managers
claims.claim: Investor interest in discretionary global macro stays high (about 50% in the survey) largely because these managers are the best storytellers with strong personalities, not because of a proven edge.
claims.indicator: SG Capital Consulting survey: strategy interest (discretionary global macro)
claims.testable: partly - compare survey interest with realised discretionary macro performance

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: in the real world I I certainly think that there's a lot more interest in in multi Strat than there is in CTA Trend
claims.claim: In the survey CTA trend ranked consistently about 3rd to 6th of 12-15 strategies, close to multi-strategy, yet in real assets multi-strat firms attract far more money; stated survey interest does not match actual flows, so the survey is an imperfect guide.
claims.indicator: strategy interest ranking (periodic table) vs asset flows
claims.testable: partly - compare survey ranks with AUM flows

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: yesterday um which would be uh Thursday evening at 48
claims.claim: Niels' trend barometer finished at 48 (neutral) on Thursday 16 May 2024, while CTA indices were still negative for May even as MSCI World rose about 5% and the S&P 500 5.3%, i.e. trend followers lagged the equity rally.
claims.indicator: trend barometer 48; CTA indices vs equity indices, May 2024
claims.testable: yes - barometer is a published reading

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: if uh The Economist or Business Week puts it on the cover that means that there's going to be a reversal
claims.claim: Magazine covers (The Economist, Business Week) on a theme such as the end of liberalism are a late, contrarian sentiment indicator: media report the trend late, so the opposite move often follows.
claims.indicator: magazine cover themes as contrarian sentiment indicator
claims.direction: fade the theme on the cover
claims.testable: partly - magazine cover indicator studies exist

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the footsie has always been very energy heavy uh and you have other countries that are you know Tech heavy and so on so forth
claims.claim: Differences in correlation between country equity indices partly reflect sector composition (FTSE energy-heavy, other markets tech-heavy), so lower cross-country correlation is not purely a deglobalisation effect and will persist for structural reasons.
claims.indicator: cross-country equity index correlation; sector weights
claims.testable: yes - decompose index correlations into sector and country effects

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: a lot of people have been out saying well we're going to have a recession it hasn't shown up after I don't know how many two years now of an inverted yield curve
claims.claim: The inverted yield curve (Campbell Harvey's recession signal) had not produced a recession after about two years, and defenders then say a different yield curve was the right one; such shifting of the indicator shows how ambiguous macro signals are, which is why Niels prefers price, the one unambiguous series.
claims.indicator: yield curve inversion (10y-2y vs other curves)
claims.conditions: ex-post choice among several yield-curve definitions
claims.testable: yes - compare curve definitions and lead times to recession

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: people are more willing to put on risk if let's say there's lower uncertainty
claims.claim: Mark judges macro and policy uncertainty to be subjectively low in May 2024 (political uncertainty indices below two years earlier), which supports risk-taking, though it may rise into the US election; Niels objects that from a European perspective uncertainty feels high.
claims.direction: risk-on when measured uncertainty is low
claims.conditions: may change as the US election approaches
claims.testable: yes - policy uncertainty index versus subsequent returns
